r7.requirement: 把 12V 降到 5V，最大负载电流 500mA；输入电压在 10.8V–13.2V 之间变化、负载电流在 100mA–500mA 之间跳变时，输出都要保持在 5V±3% 以内

rounds.diagnosis: Initial design, so there are no native results yet. I did not simulate this netlist, and the expected values below are hand estimates. The 5 V ±3% band is ±150 mV. The R1/R2 tolerance alone moves the output by about ±0.1 V, so margin is tight and I centred the nominal output near 4.98 V. There is no efficiency or ripple requirement and no output capacitor in the testbench, so I chose a linear series regulator. It has no switching ripple and is insensitive to the ±5% R/L/C variation.
rounds.changes: Series-pass linear regulator built from discrete parts. Q4 (TIP31-class NPN) is the pass emitter-follower and Q3 (BD139-class NPN) is its driver, which together form a Darlington. Q2 (2N3904-class NPN) is a common-emitter error amplifier. Its emitter sits on a 3.3 V zener reference (DZ1), biased from vin through RZ. Its base takes the output divider, R1 over R2a+R2b. Its collector load RC from vin drives the Darlington base. The loop forces mid-node = Vz + Vbe, about 3.99 V, so Vout is about 4.98 V (hand estimate), with loop gain of a few hundred. CC (47 nF) on the Q2 collector sets a dominant pole for stability. C1 (100 µF with 0.1 ohm ESR as RPAR_C1) on the output provides the filtering and load-step reservoir, since the testbench has no output cap. RPD gives the driver a minimum bias current, and the divider acts as a roughly 1 mA preload.

rounds.diagnosis: Round 1 was rejected before simulation with PORT_NOT_CONNECTED_IN_DUT: vout. The frozen spec names the ports vin, vout and gnd, but I used an internal node called 'out' for the regulator output, so the vout port was left unconnected. This was a naming error and says nothing about the circuit itself, so no performance numbers exist yet.
rounds.changes: I kept the topology and only renamed the output node from 'out' to 'vout' everywhere, including the divider top, the pass emitter, the pull-down and the output capacitor. The circuit is a Darlington emitter-follower pass stage driven by a common-emitter error amplifier that references a 3.3 V zener. Hand estimate, not simulated: Q2 collector current is about 4.2–5.3 mA over the Vin range, so Vbe is about 0.69 V and the zener sits at about 3.35 V. That puts the divider tap at about 4.04 V and Vout at about 4.04 × (1 + 1k/4.2k) ≈ 5.0 V. The divider ratio is small, so ±5% resistor tolerance moves Vout by only about ±0.05 V. The 100 µF output capacitor with 0.1 ohm ESR handles the 400 mA load steps, and CC gives a dominant pole at the amplifier output.

rounds.diagnosis: Round 2 passed all nominal checks (vout 4.909–5.018 V) but failed 1 of 40 tolerance cases. In mc_005, vout_min fell to 4.841 V against a 4.85 V limit. The cause is the resistive divider, which sets Vout = (Vz+Vbe)·(1+R1/(R2A+R2B)), a gain of about 1.24. Its ±5% R tolerances shift the ratio by about ±1.6%, which is about ±65 mV at the 4 V reference. In mc_005, R1 was -3.1% and R2A/R2B were +5%/+3.6%, which pulled Vout down by about 70 mV from a nominal minimum of 4.909 V. The nominal output also sat about 60 mV below 5.0 V, so there was little margin.
rounds.changes: I removed the divider (R1, R2A, R2B). The error amplifier's base now connects straight to vout, so Vout = Vz + Vbe(Q2) and no R tolerance sets the output voltage. The zener model is now a ~4.3 V part (BV=4.24 with RS=10 and ~5 mA bias, so Vz is about 4.30 V). With Vbe of about 0.70 V this centres Vout near 5.0 V. The remaining R tolerances (RC, RZ) only change the Q2 bias current by a few percent, which moves Vbe by about 1 mV. Loop gain rises by about 1.24x because the divider attenuation is gone, which also tightens line and load regulation. Pass stage, compensation CC and output capacitor are unchanged. Hand estimate only, not simulated.

r4.requirement: 输入 3.3V 电源，给 10Ω 负载输出 12V 直流（约 1.2A），同时输入电源的平均电流不得超过 2A

round2.reason: Energy conservation rules this out. The load needs at least 11.4^2/10 = 13.0 W at the lowest allowed output, and 14.4 W at 12 V. The input is capped at 3.3 V x 2 A = 6.6 W. Even a 100%-efficient converter would need at least 3.94 A average input current, and Round 1 measured 4.87 A at 92.9% efficiency. With 6.6 W available, the most a 10 ohm load can get is 8.12 V. Under the platform rules, internal sources are capped at 2% of input power and controlled or current sources are banned, so no other energy can make up the gap. Pre-charging capacitors during the excluded start-up window would only game the 8-10 ms measurement window and would not give continuous DC. The user must relax the input current limit (to about 5 A or more), raise the input voltage (to about 7.7 V or more at 2 A), or accept about 8 V output.
round2.diagnosis: Round 1 passed vout_regulation (12.2211 V) and vout_ripple (45.7 mV), and the platform internal-source check (0.071 W vs 0.369 W). It failed only input_current_limit: 4.87 A measured vs 2.0 A allowed. The failure comes from energy conservation, not from design quality. The measured efficiency was 92.9% (pout = 14.94 W, pin = 16.08 W). Even at the lowest allowed output (11.4 V), the load takes 11.4^2/10 = 13.0 W. The input is capped at 3.3 V x 2 A = 6.6 W. A lossless converter would still need at least 13.0 / 3.3 = 3.94 A average input current, which is 1.97x the limit. At the nominal 12 V (14.4 W) it would need at least 4.36 A. With 6.6 W in, the best possible output into 10 ohm is sqrt(6.6 x 10) = 8.12 V, well below 11.4 V. The rules close every other energy path: internal V sources are capped at 2% of testbench power (about 0.13 W at 6.6 W), there are no I/E/F/G/H/B sources, and passives are lossless at best. The only other path is pre-charging a large capacitor bank during the excluded 0-8 ms start-up window and draining it during the 8-10 ms window. That would game the measurement window rather than deliver the continuous DC the user asked for: the output would fall as soon as the stored energy ran out. It would also need at least (13.0 - 6.6) W x 2 ms = 12.8 mJ of reserve at strict +/-5% hold-up. So vout_regulation and input_current_limit cannot both pass, which matches the infeasibility note already in the frozen spec.

energy.derivation: 11.4^2/10 = 13.0 W; 3.3 V x 2 A = 6.6 W (quoted from the AI's round-2 reasoning)
